notes: Perfect claim overlap (C107-C110) regarding AFF4-CDK9 N-terminal helix interaction. Both agree on UNCERTAIN status due to observation in only one of three crystal complexes and lack of clear functional validation.

High overlap (69% Jaccard) on AFF4-CycT1 binding interface claims. Both find the crystallographic and mutagenesis data strongly supportive. Peer review explicitly affirms 'high technical quality' and 'strongly supported by extensive binding studies.'

Moderate overlap (23% Jaccard) on crystal structure determination claims (C5, C37-C38, C99-C102). Both agree structure is well-determined with acceptable statistics. Peer review notes 'crystallography appears technically strong' and 'lends confidence.'

High overlap (67% Jaccard) on functional validation of AFF4-CycT1 interface through mutagenesis (C55-C60, C88-C89). Both find mutagenesis data convincingly support the structural interface's functional importance.

High overlap (68% Jaccard) on Tat-AFF4 interaction model (C10-C11, C63-C73, C90-C91). Both find the overall model of direct Tat-AFF4 contact supported by 11-fold affinity enhancement and rescue experiments, though peer review notes some limitations addressed in R4 pairing below.

Moderate overlap (23% Jaccard) on specific Tat-AFF4 contact residues (C74-C77, C93). LLM finds evidence sufficient for SUPPORTED status, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting 'binding/rescue effects are small' for Glu61/Met62 and requesting 'additional evidence' via in vitro binding assays.

High overlap (67% Jaccard) on intersubunit pocket and Tat binding site (C78-C80, C97). LLM rates UNSUPPORTED due to lack of experimental validation of druggability claims, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional evidence but not rejecting the structural model outright.

Low overlap (33% Jaccard) on therapeutic target claims (C12, C98). LLM finds therapeutic claims UNSUPPORTED due to lack of drug screening/validation data. Peer reviewers implicitly SUPPORT by not challenging these speculative claims and acknowledging significance of findings.
Claims C81-C83, C104-C106 regarding kinase activity modulation by AFF4 and Tat appear only in LLM results. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific functional assay claims.

Minimal overlap (5% Jaccard) on claims C8-C9 regarding functional validation. Both agree on SUPPORTED status. This represents a small subset of LLM R3's broader claim set that overlaps with peer R1's comprehensive structural/functional evaluation.
